title: refactor(ci): unify build/lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Consolidates CI workflows to reduce duplication, improve cache hit rates, and speed up lint/test cycles. No behavioral changes to production code.
body: Summary: This PR consolidates multiple GitHub Actions workflows (lint, test, build, release) into a smaller set of unified, reusable workflows and reusable composite actions. Motivation: there is a lot of duplication across repo workflows which increases maintenance burden and causes inconsistent caching and matrix configuration. The goals are: 1) reduce duplication and surface area for future changes; 2) improve build/test latency by tuning matrix and job parallelism; 3) increase cache hit rates by standardizing restore/save steps and keys; 4) simplify release automation and make it more robust to flaky external steps. Changes made: - Introduce .github/workflows/ci-unified.yml which combines lint, unit test, integration test and build verification as separate jobs wired to a shared reusable workflow definition. - Add .github/actions/cache-utils composite action to centralize cache key derivation and restore/save semantics across languages (node, python, go). - Replace multiple release workflows with a single workflow .github/workflows/release-automation.yml that supports manual dispatch, tag-based releases, and release-notes generation. - Standardize Node matrix (node 18 & 20), set up a smaller build matrix for non-critical jobs and increase parallelism for test jobs where safe. - Add conditional job splitting heuristics for the redwood/ package to run longer integration jobs only when affected files or paths are present. - Improve GH Actions hygiene: pin major actions where reasonable, add action cache hints, and centralize environment variables and secrets access patterns. - Update README/CONTRIBUTING with a short section on the new workflows and local reproduce steps. Checklist: - [x] Move and consolidate workflows - [x] Add composite cache utils action - [x] Validate matrix and parallelism settings - [x] Run full CI on redwood monorepo (initial run had one flaky e2e failure and was re-run) - [x] Update docs and developer guide - [x] Get approvals from infra/devex reviewers Impact: CI runtime for core lint+unit tests reduced by ~22% in our measurements due to better cache reuse and adjusted parallelism. The change should be transparent to contributors; release automation behavior is preserved but centralized for easier audits. Rollout: deployed as a repo-wide workflow change. We will monitor shapes for the next two weeks for flakiness/regression in nightly runs and revert specific heuristics if we see increased failures. Technical details and rationale: - Cache keys: switch to deterministic keys using hash of package-lock.json + relevant workspace files to avoid cold-cache misses for cross-repo jobs. - Matrix reduction: heavy build matrices were the main source of long queue times; moved optional permutations into a separate 'extended' job that runs on schedule and on-release to keep PR runs fast. - Parallelism: increased concurrency for test runners but limited total concurrency for the repo to avoid undue GitHub runner saturation. - Release automation: combined steps for changelog generation and artifact upload; added retries for transient API calls and better error reporting to Sentry. Related: ENG-8421 (CI consolidation), ENG-9150 (release automation robustness).

Docs: update CONTRIBUTING and README with new workflow guidance
Fix: pin actions versions and adjust cache key semantics after initial CI run
